name: Compressor contactor (3-pole definite purpose)
function: 24 VAC coil pulls in three line-voltage poles to start the compressor. The control board decides when; the contactor just does the heavy switching.

location.value: Main control panel, line-voltage section. On the wiring diagram: coil in the 24V ladder fed from the M2 compressor 1 output; poles in the line-voltage section feeding B1.

lennox-lch240.sequenceRole: M2 energizes the K1 coil on a Y1 call once safeties are closed and the minimum-off timer is satisfied.

partNumber.note: Pull from the LCH parts list.

location.value: Control box, line-voltage section. Coil driven by the unit controller compressor output through the LPC/HPC safety string.

trane-tsc072.sequenceRole: Controller energizes CC1 on Y1 after the anti-short-cycle timer; CC1 also brings on the outdoor fan.

partNumber.note: Pull from the Precedent parts list.

failureModes.name: Coil open
failureModes.goodVsBad: Good coil: low tens of ohms. Open: OL with 24V present at the coil and the contactor not pulled in.
failureModes.symptoms: Compressor never starts; fans and blower may run. Board shows the compressor output on.

failureModes.name: Coil shorted
failureModes.goodVsBad: Reads near 0 Ω; often blows the 24V fuse or trips the transformer breaker on a cooling call.
failureModes.symptoms: Control fuse pops on Y call, thermostat goes blank.

failureModes.name: Contacts pitted / burned
failureModes.goodVsBad: Good: well under 0.5 V across each closed pole under load. Pitted: measurable drop and heat. One pole fully burned open = single-phasing.
failureModes.symptoms: Compressor runs hot, trips on overload, hums, or draws unbalanced amps.

failureModes.name: Contacts welded
failureModes.goodVsBad: Line voltage reaches T side with the coil de-energized.
failureModes.symptoms: Compressor runs with no call; won't shut off; can freeze the coil or run with no blower.

test.meter: DMM on VAC for coil and pole drop; Ω for coil with one lead lifted and power locked out.
procedure: With a call present, read voltage across the coil terminals. 24V and not pulled in = coil or armature problem; 0V = look upstream (board output, safeties, wiring).
Energized under load, read voltage across each pole, line to load (L1-T1, L2-T2, L3-T3). Healthy closed contacts read near zero.
LOTO, verify dead, lift one coil lead, ohm the coil.
Visual: pitting, carbon, heat discoloration, and armature travel (push it in by hand only with power locked out).
safety: Pole-drop readings are live line-voltage work: rated meter and leads, arc-flash PPE for the voltage class, one hand where practical.
Never push the armature in by hand on a live contactor.
Lift a coil lead before ohming, or you're reading the parallel circuit, not the coil.

coilOhms.note: Typical 24 VAC definite-purpose coil range. Real value is on the contactor label/spec sheet.

contactDropBadV.note: Between 0.5 and 2 V = marginal, replace soon. Over 2 V = replace now.

symptoms.customer: "Unit's running but blowing warm" or "breaker keeps tripping" (welded/shorted cases).
symptoms.tech: Blower and condenser fans may run, compressor doesn't. Board output on. Coil 24V present. Or: unbalanced amps, hot compressor, hum.

confusedWith: Open compressor internal overload (also no-start with contactor pulled in, but the contactor IS pulled in)
Open safety in the 24V string (no 24V at coil, not a contactor problem)

labCases.context: Pulled K1 during a no-cool call that turned out to be a board issue. Shop wants to know if it can go back on the truck.

tests.label: Coil resistance
tests.setup: Off the unit, on the bench.

tests.label: Pole drop under load
tests.setup: Bench rig: 24V to the coil, resistive load bank on the poles.

readings.visual: Light gray contact faces, no pitting, armature moves freely.

labCases.explanation: Coil inside the typical range and every pole drops ≤0.2 V under load. Good part.

labCases.context: No-cool call. 24.9 V measured across the K1 coil, contactor not pulled in. Pulled for bench test.

readings.visual: Coil body slightly darkened near one terminal.

labCases.explanation: OL across the coil = open winding. That's why 24 V was present and nothing happened.

labCases.context: PM visit. Compressor running fine, but you take pole drops on CC1 while you're in there.
labCases.explanation: Pole 2 drops 1.2 V under load. That's heat and wasted power, but not failed yet. Quote it as replace-soon.

labCases.context: Compressor tripping on overload. Contactor pulled in when you arrive.
labCases.explanation: 96 V across a closed pole means it isn't making contact. The compressor is single-phasing on that leg. Replace the contactor, then check the compressor.
